First, notice that we can factor out $5$ from each of the terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{b}^{2}-15b+10 & =5({b}^{2}-3b+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial ${b}^{2}-3b+2$ in parentheses.

We start by listing the factor pairs of the constant term $(2).$ We will want to find the factor pair that also adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-3),$ so we will consider the negative factor pairs in particular:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1) & \times (-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)+(-2) & =-3 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Using the factor pair identified above, we write the linear term as $-3b=-b-2b$ and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}^{2}-3b+2 & = \\ {b}^{2}-b-2b+2 & = \\ ({b}^{2}-b)+(-2b+2) & = \\ b(b-1)-2(b-1) & = \\ (b-2)(b-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5({b}^{2}-3b+2) & =5(b-2)(b-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $p=-2,q=-1,$ and $p+q=-3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{t}^{2}-15t-20 & =5({t}^{2}-3t-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial ${t}^{2}-3t-4$ in parentheses.

First, we find the factor pairs of the constant term $(-4).$ The constant term is negative, so that means one of the factors is negative and the other is positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \times (-4) \\ (-1) & \times 4 \\ 2 & \times (-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+(-4) & =-3 & ✓ \\ (-1)+4 & =3 & \times  \\ 2+(-2) & =0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

Using the factor pair identified above, we write the linear term as $-3t=t-4t$ and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-3t-4 & = \\ {t}^{2}+t-4t-4 & = \\ ({t}^{2}+t)+(-4t-4) & = \\ t(t+1)-4(t+1) & = \\ (t-4)(t+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5({t}^{2}-3t-4) & =5(t-4)(t+1)\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that we can factor out a $-3$ from each of the terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{a}^{2}+30a-72 & =-3({a}^{2}-10a+24)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial ${a}^{2}-10a+24$ in parentheses.

First, we find the factor pairs of the constant term $(24).$ We will want to find the factor pair that also adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-10),$ so we will consider the negative factor pairs in particular:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1) & \times (-24) \\ (-2) & \times (-12) \\ (-3) & \times (-8) \\ (-4) & \times (-6)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-10):$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)+(-24) & =-25 & \times  \\ (-2)+(-12) & =-14 & \times  \\ (-3)+(-8) & =-11 & \times  \\ (-4)+(-6) & =-10 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

 

Using the factor pair identified in the previous step, write the linear term as $-10a=-4a-6a,$ and then factor the expression completely:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3({a}^{2}-10a+24) & = \\ -3({a}^{2}-4a-6a+24) & = \\ -3(a(a-4)-6(a-4)) & = \\ -3(a-4)(a-6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-4,q=-6,$ and $p+q=-10.$

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \times (-2) \\ (-1) & \times 2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(1):$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can factor out a $3$ from each of the terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-21x+30 & = \\ 3({x}^{2}-7x+10)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial $x^2-7x+10$ in parentheses.

We start by listing the factor pairs of the constant term $(10),$ but only the negative factor pairs since the coefficient of the linear term $(-7)$ is negative.

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1,-10),\,(-2,-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-7)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)+(-10) & =-11 & \times  \\ (-2)+(-5) & =-7 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

 

Using the factor pair identified above, we write the linear term as $-7x=-2x-5x,$ and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-7x+10 & = \\ {x}^{2}-2x-5x+10 & = \\ ({x}^{2}-2x)+(-5x+10) & = \\ x(x-2)-5(x-2) & = \\ (x-5)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
3\left(x^2-7x+10\right)&=\[5pt]
3(x-5)(x-2)
	}
$$

                    Factoring a Trinomial With a Negative Quadratic Term
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can factor out a $-2$ from each of the terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}-22x-48 & = \\ -2({x}^{2}+11x+24)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial $x^2+11x+24$ in parentheses.

First, we find the factor pairs of the constant term $(24)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1,24),\,(2,12),\,(3,8),\,(4,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(11)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+24 & =25 & \times  \\ 2+12 & =14 & \times  \\ 3+8 & =11 & ✓ \\ 4+6 & =10 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

 

Using the factor pair identified in the previous step, write the linear term as $11x=3x+8x,$ and then factor the expression completely:

$$
\eqalign{
-2\left(x^2+11x+24\right)&=\[5pt]
-2\left(x^2+3x+8x+24\right)&=\[5pt]
-2\left((x^2+3x)+(8x+24)\right)&=\[5pt]
-2\Bigl(x(x+3)+8(x+3)\Bigr)&=\[5pt]
-2(x+8)(x+3)
	}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose we want to factor the polynomial 

$$
8x^2 + 24x + 16.
$$

At first glance, it looks tricky because the coefficients are rather large! 

However, notice that all the terms have a common factor of $8.$ If we first factor out an $8$ from each of the terms, then we can cut the factoring down to something more manageable:

$$
\eqalign{
		8x^2 + 24x + 16 &= \[5pt]
		8(x^2 + 3x + 2)
	}
$$

Now, we need to factor the polynomial $x^2 + 3x + 2$ in the parentheses.

The constant term $(2)$ has a single factor pair, namely

$$
(1, 2).
$$

 

Notice that the numbers in this factor pair indeed sum to the linear term's coefficient $(1+2=3).$ 

So, we can write the linear term as $3x=x+2x$ and factor as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+3x+2 & = \\ {x}^{2}+x+2x+2 & = \\ ({x}^{2}+x)+(2x+2) & = \\ x(x+1)+2(x+1) & = \\ (x+2)(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}^{2}+24x+16 & = \\ 8({x}^{2}+3x+2) & = \\ 8(x+2)(x+1) & \end{aligned}
$$
